images.title: Smaller numbers, same length
images.purpose: Show that dividing the top and the bottom of 6/8 by the same number gives 3/4, and the shaded length of the strip does not change.
images.composition: Two strips of the same length stacked with a wide gap, a fraction to the left of each, and one downward arrow between the fractions.
images.exact_structure: Upper strip: cut into 8 equal parts, the left 6 filled teal #0072B2, with 6/8 to its left. Lower strip: exactly the same length, left and right edges lined up, cut into 4 equal parts, the left 3 filled amber #E69F00, with 3/4 to its left. The shaded parts of both strips end at exactly the same place. One reddish purple #CC79A7 downward arrow from 6/8 to 3/4, labelled beside it. A short note centred at the bottom. Exactly 2 strips, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any on-screen controls, panels or app frame, or shaded parts that end at different places
images.takeaway: Dividing the top and the bottom by the same number gives smaller numbers for the same length.
images.description: A strip in 8 equal parts with 6 teal labelled 6/8, above a strip of the same length in 4 equal parts with 3 amber labelled 3/4; an arrow marked ÷ 2 top and bottom joins them.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at where both shaded parts end and say that 6/8 and 3/4 are the same length.

image_decisions.why: The practice divides top and bottom while the strip stays the same length; one strip picture sets up that idea.
